body.x: Deep-fusion AI Inc., led by CEO Sunghun Yu, participated in CES 2025, held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas, under the Incheon IFEZ Pavilion. The company aims to revolutionize autonomous driving by offering cost-effective 4D imaging radar solutions as alternatives to expensive LiDAR systems. It has developed applications such as 360-degree deep learning and HD maps, integrating them into proprietary controllers offered as complete solutions. The innovative approach to 4D imaging radar deep learning has been demonstrated on vehicles from multiple global automakers.

At CES 2025, Deep-fusion AI showcased its flagship 360-degree deep learning for 4D imaging radar. Unlike optical sensors like cameras or LiDAR, radar-based sensors lack standardized datasets for deep learning. To address this, the company created pre-training models by simulating 4D imaging radar in virtual environments tailored to various manufacturers’ specifications. This approach allows radar manufacturers to meet performance benchmarks and enables automakers to adopt tailored solutions for specific vehicle models upon product release.

The innovative platform developed by Deep-fusion AI enables automakers to select 4D imaging radar solutions based on mounting location, cost, and intended use. A representative from the company highlighted the company’s goal of fostering collaborative projects with radar and automotive manufacturers. The company showcased real-time robot deep-learning recognition and spatial mapping using 4D imaging radar. The demonstration emphasized its potential as a cost-effective alternative to LiDAR solutions.

Deep-fusion AI plans to launch a series of advanced solutions in 2025. These include a 4D imaging radar controller equipped with recognition functions for vehicle autonomous driving and auto valet parking, a radar controller with recognition capabilities for autonomous maritime navigation and docking systems, and a comprehensive sensor module combining multiple 4D imaging radars and cameras for autonomous navigation.

Deep-fusion AI’s participation in CES 2025 highlights its commitment to driving autonomous and robotics innovation. The company aims to expand its influence by delivering high-performance solutions tailored to global market demands.

body.x: AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
